Each row goes through the same validation, cycle check, events and audit as POST /api/plans. A row is matched to an existing plan by its stable key, in this order: pid; a globally-unique external identifier (Jira key, Asana gid, Trello id, MS Project id, GitHub project id, Linear id, URI, UUID); owner_org_id plus code (a bare code is not a key). A keyless row is checked for duplicates and, if it looks like one, held in the review queue (provenance import) rather than created or merged (on_keyless=create skips the check). One bad row never aborts the load, and the counts always reconcile: created + updated + unchanged + queued_for_review + failed equals total. post.description: gate_readiness (feedforward, fixed at 100%), work_in_progress (concurrent, caller-supplied limit), cycle_time_p85 (concurrent, caller-supplied SLE calendar days), and budget_variance (feedback, defaults to a 10% tolerance). Opt-in and per-plan, never automatic: a feedforward control's whole design intent is to be able to block a write once something enforces that, so silently registering one on every plan would be an unrequested behavioural change. work_in_progress_limit and cycle_time_p85_days have no default (both are plan-specific; inventing one would be the exact risk this endpoint exists to avoid) and are required. Idempotent per metric: one already registered and enabled is reported already_registered rather than duplicated. Retrospectives are deliberately not included — no metric exists for 'a retrospective happened' and this endpoint does not invent one.

caller-supplied parameter rather than a crate-wide constant,
because a cycle-time SLE is a per-plan commitment, not a fact

Per currency, never added across: the budget (sum of planned amounts), mean, cost at P10/P50/P80/P90, the share at or under the budget (budget_confidence_bp), a histogram, a per-line sensitivity correlation, how often each event struck. Seeded: the same seed gives the same result; with no uncertainty every percentile is the budget. Assumptions are echoed, including that inputs are independent (no correlation). A link to a plan the caller may NOT read (private and not a member, or not granted) is left out of the calculation and appears only in restricted_edges as an 'external dependency (restricted)' with the edge id and this plan's own task: nothing about the other side. Up to 8 linked plans and 3000 tasks are followed (external_truncated says when more existed). Forward and backward pass over the plan's task network: early and late start and finish, total float (how long before the project finish moves), free float (how long before a successor is delayed), critical (float 0) and near-critical (?near= business days, default 5), and every critical chain along driving edges. All four relationship types (fs, ss, ff, sf) with a lag or lead. Edges are the dependencies between the plan's tasks plus task precedes relations. A task's planned start is a lower bound: pushed_days says by how many business days its predecessors force it later than planned. A task with no duration, or with no start and no scheduled predecessor, is listed unscheduled with the reason, never given a float of zero. A dependency cycle is a 422. Business days use the plan's calendar (all seven days until SC-2).

get.description: Inputs: the plan's tasks, dependencies and calendars, who each unfinished task is assigned to, people's availability and their bookings in other plans. The schedule is first levelled for people's time as in the leveling proposal, with critical tasks allowed to move (so the finish may move; finish_delay_days says by how much). The chain is then the longest path, by summed business-day duration, through finish-to-start dependencies that held a task back and resource links (a task started the day its person came free), ending on the project's last day. crosses_paths is true when the chain uses a resource link, which means it is not the critical path; each task says whether it is on the critical path, which is returned beside it, computed from dependencies alone on the schedule as entered, and never blended with the chain. Ties: the earlier task in the input wins and tied_chains says another chain was as long. With no assigned unfinished task the answer is state no_critical_chain with reason no_assignments (or no_scheduled_tasks), never a guess. Only finish-to-start dependencies are followed as links and a milestone is not a resource link. A person is named only to a caller who may manage them; anyone else sees person-N.

get.description: Inputs: the plan's tasks, dependencies, calendars and assignments, each task's aggressive and safe estimate (see ccpm-estimates; the estimate rule in force is echoed), people's availability and their bookings elsewhere. Tasks are scheduled at their aggressive estimate where they have one (the rest keep their likely duration and are listed under scheduled_at_likely_duration), levelled for people's time, and the critical chain is found as for critical-chain. The project buffer sits at the end of the chain; a feeding buffer sits where a chain of other tasks joins it, each task belonging to one feeding chain. A buffer is sized from the safety removed from its tasks (safe minus aggressive) by buffer_rule (cut_and_paste: half, rounded up; root_sum_squares: the root of the sum of squares, rounded up; PROJECT_PORTFOLIO_MANAGEMENT_BUFFER_RULE, echoed with a flag if the setting was unusable), in business days of the plan's calendar. A feeding buffer larger than the room before its join reports would_push_chain and push_days; it is never absorbed. Resource buffers are readiness alerts for assigned chain tasks, alert_on being resource_buffer_lead_days business days before the start (PROJECT_PORTFOLIO_MANAGEMENT_RESOURCE_BUFFER_DAYS, default 2); a person is named only to a caller who may manage them. With no chain, or a chain task lacking an estimate, the answer is state no_buffers with the reason (no_assignments, no_scheduled_tasks or estimates_missing) and the tasks, never a guess; a feeding chain with a task lacking an estimate has no size and says so.

get.description: Planned value follows the phased budget baseline (the latest version in each currency; linear within a period, the standard EVM convention). Earned value is the budget times the plan's PHYSICAL percent complete: each task is counted 0/100, 0/50/100, or by a person-entered percent (always flagged, always with a note), weighted equally or by story points (the plan default, PUT …/earned-value-settings). Actual cost is, by default, the plan's recorded budget-line actuals in that currency; ?ac=labour uses recorded labour cost instead (time entries x the rate in force, the rate stored with each; a currency with none recorded has no actual cost, null, never zero) and ?ac=both adds the two, which is only right when the budget lines do not already include labour. The response names the source in ac_source. ac=labour and ac=both are finance data and need finance access (403 otherwise); the forecast, S-curve, snapshots and portfolio figures still use budget-line actuals. Ratios are basis points (10000 = 1.0), money minor units, all integer. SPI(t) is earned schedule over actual time and, unlike SPI, still says so when a project finishes late. Undefined figures are null with a reason (no_planned_value_yet, no_actuals_recorded, no_planned_value), never zero or 1.0; with no baseline the answer is blocks null, absent no_baseline; with nothing to weigh, no_weighted_tasks. Measured as of today (UTC date): actuals carry no date, so the past is not reconstructed. Currencies never merge: budget lines in a currency with no baseline are listed in unbaselined_currencies.

None is presented as the answer: `recommended` is a stated rule (cost efficiency continues when the schedule is on track; both pressures when it is behind the amber line; the one-off reading when there is no CPI) and the others are returned beside it. TCPI to the budget and to the recommended forecast: above 1.00 the remaining work must be done more efficiently than the work so far; a target already spent is budget_exhausted, never infinity. A missing denominator is null with undefined_denominator, never zero. Traffic lights use thresholds from PROJECT_PORTFOLIO_MANAGEMENT_EV_THRESHOLDS (spi_cpi_amber, spi_cpi_red, tcpi_amber, tcpi_red, in basis points), shown in the response with their source.
